acceptance_criteria.criterion: After `Set`, the value persisted via `ISettingsService` is the new mode and re-instantiating the service emits the persisted value as `Current`.
`LoggingSetup.ConfigureSerilog` produces a logger whose minimum level matches the mapping 1→Warning, 2→Information, 3→Debug, 4→Verbose; values outside 1–4 clamp to the nearest in-range level.
The configured rolling file sink targets `<AppData>/VideoIndexer/logs/videoindexer-.log` with a 14-day retention policy.

summary: Added Serilog.Extensions.Hosting, Serilog.Sinks.Console, Serilog.Sinks.File packages to VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.csproj.

Implemented ThemeService (IThemeService): reads initial theme from ISettingsService.Current, Set(mode) updates Current + persists via SaveAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult() + raises ThemeChanged exactly once.

Implemented LoggingSetup.ConfigureSerilog: static method mapping verbosity 1-4 to Warning/Information/Debug/Verbose (Math.Clamp for out-of-range), Console sink, daily rolling File sink at <LogsDirectory>/videoindexer-.log with 14-day retention.
dotnet build -c Release: clean, zero warnings.

comments.note: ThemeService.Set calls SaveAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult() — the sync-over-async anti-pattern. Acceptable here: theme changes are user-initiated, infrequent, and the write is <1 KB. If async UI patterns are ever adopted (e.g., ReactiveUI), ThemeService should be refactored to expose an async SetAsync method.

LoggingSetup.MapVerbosity is a public static method, which allows unit testing the verbosity mapping in isolation. This is a deliberate design choice for testability — the QA can test MapVerbosity directly without constructing Serilog infrastructure.

The unreachable default arm in the MapVerbosity switch statement is required by the compiler (exhaustiveness). Its presence is intentional but slightly odd after Math.Clamp. A code comment explains this.

summary: Reviewed 3 production files (ThemeService.cs, LoggingSetup.cs, VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.csproj). 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Low, 1 Info finding. All OWASP Top 10 categories assessed. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Low — A03/A05 (Injection / Security Misconfiguration): src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Logging/LoggingSetup.cs — options.Logging.FilePath is used as a Serilog file sink path without sanitization (line ~30: var logFilePath = options.Logging.FilePath ?? Path.Combine(...)). A crafted config value could redirect log output to a UNC share (\\attacker\share\log.log) or an arbitrary local path via path traversal. Risk is self-inflicted in a desktop app where the user controls their own config file. Remediation: if the config is ever exposed to untrusted input (e.g., multi-user profiles or remote config), validate FilePath against an allowlist of permitted base directories before use.

Info — A09 (Security Logging): src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Logging/LoggingSetup.cs — the Console sink is unconditionally active (WriteTo.Console()). At verbosity 4 (Verbose), all log events including potentially sensitive data flow to stdout. For a desktop app this is acceptable; however, consider gating the Console sink on a debug/development flag if the application is ever deployed in a context where stdout is captured or forwarded.

No additional security findings. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed across all 3 modified production files. No Critical or High issues identified. Dependency versions (Serilog 8.0.0/6.0.0, Microsoft.Extensions.* 8.0.0-8.0.2) have no known CVEs at these releases.

summary: Reviewed 3 production files (ThemeService.cs, LoggingSetup.cs, VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.csproj) and 3 test files (ThemeServiceTests.cs, LoggingSetupTests.cs, VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests.csproj).
No blocking issues found. All 4 ACs are correctly fulfilled by the implementation.

ThemeService: sealed, correct IThemeService implementation, event raised after persist — subtle ordering concern if SaveAsync throws (Current updated but ThemeChanged not fired), but non-blocking for a desktop app with trivial writes.

LoggingSetup: clean static class, MapVerbosity correctly public for testability, Math.Clamp approach is idiomatic, retainedFileCountLimit:14 + RollingInterval.Day correctly satisfies the 14-day retention spec.

Tests: 21 passing, well-named, appropriate coverage. Minor Moq fragility in one test (Invocations.Clear instead of new mock). net10.0 test target vs net8.0 production target is a documented host constraint workaround — APIs used are stable across both versions.
Two documentation-forward items tagged for the Documentation agent. One low-priority debt note forwarded from Developer (sync-over-async) confirmed in scope.

comments.note: ThemeService.Set() ordering: _current is set before SaveAsync is called. If SaveAsync throws (e.g. disk full), Current reflects the new mode but ThemeChanged has not fired, leaving subscribers with stale visual state. Non-blocking for a desktop app with trivial writes, but worth noting for future async refactor context. Alternative: persist first, then update _current and raise event — this keeps state consistent on failure.

LoggingSetupTests.cs — ConfigureSerilog_LogFilePathContainsVideoIndexerFilename uses appPathsMock.Invocations.Clear() to reset invocation counts mid-test. This pattern accesses Moq internals and is fragile. Prefer splitting into two separate test methods or creating a fresh Mock<IAppPaths> for the second assertion. Non-blocking since tests pass, but reduces future maintainability.

Target framework mismatch: production projects (VideoIndexer.Core, VideoIndexer.Infrastructure) target net8.0 while tests target net10.0. QA documented this as a host constraint workaround (.NET 8 runtime absent). BCL APIs used (Path.Combine, Math.Clamp, record with-expressions) are stable across both — tests are valid. Recommend aligning targets when the host runtime is available to ensure precise fidelity.

LoggingSetup.MapVerbosity is public static purely for unit testability. An alternative is internal + [assembly: InternalsVisibleTo("VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests")]. Either approach is valid; the current public choice means callers can also use it to inspect the effective log level for a given verbosity setting, which has minor utility. No change required.

[documentation-forward] ThemeService class XML doc mentions sync-over-async as acceptable but does not document the exception-safety ordering in Set(). Add a remarks comment explaining that if SaveAsync throws, Current will reflect the new mode but ThemeChanged will not have fired — callers should not rely on Current/ThemeChanged consistency in error paths.

[documentation-forward] LoggingSetup.ConfigureSerilog XML doc does not mention the 14-day rolling file retention or that retainedFileCountLimit maps to calendar days only when the app runs every day. Add a remarks note clarifying that 14 files are retained, one per rolling day, which approximates 14-day retention when the app runs daily.
